Work through one whole culture group at a time, including all linked subcultures. Each child needs a distinct main subject or symbol: pose, taper, fold or colour changes to the same object are insufficient. Retain family resemblance through a shared medium, format and palette. Ground subjects in real objects, geography or nature, and identify new artistic motifs as proposals rather than inventing ethnic crests, traditional patterns or occupational stereotypes. Flags may guide colours only. Canadian uses animals, Brazilian uses birds, and British uses pub-sign-inspired imagery; existing British icons are obsolete placeholders. Use one to three useful, verified Commons file-page references per brief, counting AI links and live GFX Image links together. Do not pad siblings with repeated pictures of a common frame or duplicate one image through multiple URL forms.
